domain_reasoning: Most time goes into building cost and volume analysis in spreadsheets and comparing against payer schedules and market rates.

review_reasoning: Finance leadership checks the assumptions and spot-checks the numbers; a full schedule needs several rates traced to cost data.

context_reasoning: Needs the facility's cost structure, payer contracts and charge master conventions, learned over weeks.
match_reasoning: Finch items are finance workflows using spreadsheets across workbooks with a written output, sharing the analysis-and-summarise actions, but they are not pricing proposals. GDPval has professional deliverables from a brief but not rate setting specifically.
best_difference: general finance workflows rather than pricing proposals tied to payer and cost data

domain_reasoning: The time goes into running energy models, calculations and lifecycle assessment tools, then collating results.

match_reasoning: JobBench items are professional analysis requests with source files and a checklist of expert criteria, sharing the compute-and-report actions. They are not specific to mechanical energy modelling.
best_difference: technical analysis on public-record files in other fields, not engineering simulation of a design
